extracted.intended_audience: education policymakers, school governors, Board of Education officials, and educators interested in governance and reform of endowed/secondary schools (early 20th-century UK context)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for assessing and reforming endowed grammar and public schools: their governance, admission policies, financial endowments, and the proper division of responsibilities between local and central authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devolution with reserved central functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility should be devolved to local education committees, with reservation to the central authority of certain functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, training of teachers and the inspection of schools as regards conditions of health should remain central functions; local authorities should supply statistical information required by the Board. Aim to 'make the most of the advantages, and to minimise the evils, of centralisation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of governors and financial accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Each endowed school should have a board of governors, including members representing the local authority, and management should be entrusted to the governors by the scheme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While management rests with governors, it should be their duty to present a yearly budget to the supervising body. This emphasizes local representation plus transparency and annual financial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit pooling/redistribution of endowments to preserve local benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any pooling and re-distribution of endowments should be so limited as to preserve the benefits of each foundation to the area of the local authority in which it exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach would reduce opposition to transferring endowments from village to populous centres and still 'fulfil in a reasonable manner the intention of the pious founder.' Municipalisation of small endowments (e.g., Derby precedent) is recommended to make funds more generally available while keeping local benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeted small additions to improve efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: A comparatively small addition to the funds of a struggling school can often make a relatively enormous increase in its efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy-makers should prioritize targeted top-ups to weak schools rather than assuming large-scale redistribution will solve systemic funding problems; investigate precise sums available before major redistribution schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve traditions of leading public schools; reform cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Leading public schools are national assets with unrivalled traditions and their constitutions should not be destroyed for comparatively trivial pecuniary gain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reforms should be cautious: consider 'some mild infusion of democratic influence' (e.g., admission of fit boys from every social rank) while avoiding wholesale dismantling of traditions. Balance national benefit against preserving institutional character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority of educational advantage in schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: "In making a scheme regard shall be had primarily to the educational advantages to be derived from the scheme." (Clause 16)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Board or commissioners devise or amend schemes for endowed schools, the primary test should be the educational advantage produced. Safeguards (e.g., for religious character) may be included, but educational benefit is the principal consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for founder's intentions vs present needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the classes now enjoying benefits are the same as those for whom the endowments were originally intended and whether maintenance of local privileges is justified by respect for founder's intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clarendon Commission noted difficulty in assigning a precise meaning to 'poverty' and suggested the qualification of indigence may be practically inoperative; policy should weigh original intentions against present social realities and the wider public good.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guard against local privileges that no longer serve sufficient reason
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether maintenance of local privileges (e.g., right to gratuitous education for local residents attracted by cheap education) is recommended either by respect for founder's intentions or by any other sufficient reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The view expressed is that, in many cases, such privileges are not justified and need not be preserved if they conflict with broader educational objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal/administrative standards governing staff tenure
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the law of 1869, head and assistant masters are dismissible 'at pleasure' in nearly all endowed schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a factual/legal standard noted as part of the governance regime; reformers should consider the implications for staff security and professional standards when amending schemes or transferring powers between charity and education authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central control over grant-aided schools will increase and must be managed
rubrics_metrics.description: Control exercised by the Board of Education over schools aided by grants of public money has greatly increased and is destined to become more penetrating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers should seek to maximise the advantages and minimise the evils of increased bureaucratic influence: encourage local public interest and a strong profession of teachers to counterbalance centralisation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify procedure and expand scheme-making powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Education should be conferred enlarged powers to make new schemes and to amend old ones, with considerable simplification of procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II of the (1906) Education Bill proposed such enlargement and simplification; pragmatic legal procedural reform is recommended to enable effective, timely changes to school schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect religious character and institutional exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Safeguards relating to the religious character of certain foundations should be introduced; universities and their colleges may be excluded from broad reforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When drafting schemes or reforms, include provisions to protect the historic religious character of foundations where appropriate and respect reasonable exceptions for long-established institutions (e.g., Eton, Winchester, universities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Realistic assessment of endowment resources and limits of redistribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The sums available in endowments are far less than is often supposed and the Roby Return and other sources do not always specify educational portions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In planning redistribution or relying on endowments for relief, perform careful audit and analysis (Roby Return, Bryce Commission notes); avoid overestimating available funds and recognize redistribution alone cannot supply large community relief.
